newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse proposes new membership rules.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse proposes new membership rules.

text.p: The Zagreb Stock Exchange will present new rules to its 45 member brokerages on Monday in another step to improve the regulation of Croatia's small but expanding share market, spokesman Zeljko Kardum said.
"The market conditions have changed since the old rules were passed," Kardum told Reuters. "We have to coordinate them with new corporate and securities legislation."
If brokers accept the proposal, fresh membership rules will come into force later this month, he said.
The main goal is to make the Croatian market safer for investors by improving a code of ethics for traders to prevent price rigging and similar internal deals, Kardum said.
One set of brakes was built into a new on-line trading system TEST 1.5 launched by the bourse last month.
It disables deals which have been prearranged at a much higher price than the prevailing market price by forcing the bidder to buy all other shares offered at a lower price first.
So far 24 brokerage houses have obtained a direct link with the central bourse brain, but more are interested in it.
Fresh regulations are also necessary for admitting new members from a growing number of foreign banks and their brokerage units, opening almost monthly in Croatia.
The bourse used to lease member slots but this is no longer possible and each brokerage has to become a member to be allowed to trade.
"We have some pending requests from (traders) that are expecting a licence from the securities commission," Kardum said.
The last one to be admitted as a member in summer 1996 was a brokerage registered at Austria's Raiffeisenbank subsidiary in Zagreb.
The bourse now has 34 founders, not all of whom are its members, and it aims to gradually change that.
"By 1999, our shareholder and member structures will have to be the same," Kardum said.

Otherwise, the new rules contained nothing "revolutionary" or unusual, he said. "What we are trying to do is polish the regulations and raise their level in line with that existing elsewhere in the world."
The Zagreb bourse has very strict listing requirements for its top flight shares designed according to London Stock Exchange rules. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
